newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher, wheat seen as motivator.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher, wheat seen as motivator.

text.p: Uncertainty over the extent of freeze damage to the U.S. wheat crop and earlier gains in that market helped push CBOT soybean futures to a modestly higher close Monday, floor traders said.
"I think the soybean market won't go much lower or higher until we find out the extent of the damage to the wheat crop," said one veteran floor trader.

CBOT grain trade on Tuesday was very nervous and choppy as assessments of wheat freeze damage continue to eke out of Kansas, Texas and Oklahoma. Many in the trade are unwilling to make large trades until the full damage is known, they said.
"This is still all about wheat," said a commission house trader. "We're seeing sideways trade in a range-bound market. and the spreads continue to unwind."
Liquidation before first notice day on April 30 limited advances in the May contract.
Continued talk that a commercial firm was unloading soybeans from Brazil at the U.S. Gulf also weighed on the spot contract, floor traders said.
CBOT soybeans ended 3-1/2 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 4-1/2 at $8.43 and May up 3-1/2 at $8.40-1/2 per bushel.
Ideas that Monday's losses in CBOT soybean futures were overdone pushed the market to modest gains at midsession Tuesday, floor traders said.
"There's nothing going on down here," said one floor trader. "We're just oversold."
Soybeans were lower near the open, but a big purchase by Merrill Lynch was also said to spur some additional buying. Merrill Lynch bought 2.5 million bushels July, traders said.
The market continued to find support from ideas that U.S. soybean supplies are at low levels, and on ideas that South American crops will come in lower-than-expected.
"There are some legitimate concerns about losses down there," one Chicago-based analyst said. "The Brazilian crop is more like a 26 (million tonne) crop than a 27."
Dry weather at the tail-end of the growing season in Brazil Argentina were expected to cut production in both those countries.
May soybeans labored under pressure from liquidation in front of first notice day on April 30, traders said.
At 1117 CDT, CBOT soybeans were down 1-1/2 to up 3-1/2 cents per bushel, with July down one at $8.37-1/2, and May was down two at $8.35 per bushel.
